structure.note: Class A and Class B have one vote per share and identical economic rights, but vote separately to elect directors: Class A elects most of the board (eight of the eleven nominees in 2026, Class B three). Swoosh, LLC holds 78.8% of Class A. Phil Knight has no voting rights over Swoosh; the 10-K says his son Travis Knight, a director, 'has a significant role in the management of the Class A Common Stock owned by Swoosh, LLC.' 'controlled' is false: no person or entity holds over 50% of all votes (on matters other than director elections the classes vote together, one vote per share, and Knight entities hold well under half), and neither filing calls Nike a controlled company. Through Class A, however, Knight entities effectively decide most board seats.

notes: Fiscal year ended May 31, 2026 (Nike's fiscal 2026; matches data.js fy 'May 2026'). Documents read on sec.gov: FY2026 Form 10-K (accession 0000320187-26-000088, filed July 15, 2026) and 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0000320187-26-000089), ownership as of June 30, 2026. Phil Knight is Chairman Emeritus with a standing invitation to attend board meetings as a non-voting observer (2026 proxy). OWNERSHIP: the proxy states percentages only per class, and its Class B column assumes each holder's Class A has been converted, so no figure in the table is a share of all common stock. Phil Knight's economic share is therefore given only as leader.derived (2.41%). The family field holds Swoosh, LLC with pctEconomic null: the proxy gives it 78.8% of Class A and 15.6% of Class B on an as-converted basis (221,750,000 shares, per a Form 4 as of December 30, 2025, down from 226,750,000), but no share of all common stock, and recomputing it is not allowed. The proxy says the table 'contains substantial duplications in the numbers of shares and percentages of Class A and Class B Stock shown for Swoosh, LLC, Philip Knight, and the Travis A. Knight 2009 Irrevocable Trust II'. Philip Knight's line excludes Swoosh's shares, and Travis Knight disclaims Swoosh's shares. The Travis A. Knight 2009 Irrevocable Trust II (24,681,369 Class A, 8.8% of Class A) is another Knight family holder; it is not added to the family figure or listed as a holder. LARGEST HOLDERS left empty on purpose: Vanguard Capital Management (89,476,687 shares, 7.5% of Class B) and State Street (59,588,679 shares, 5.0% of Class B), both per 13G/A filings as of March 31, 2026, are stated only as percentages of Class B, not of all shares. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line covers common and preferred together. Nike's only preferred stock is 300,000 redeemable preferred shares held by Sojitz, so the line is effectively common dividends, and XBRL tags it PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock. BUYBACKS: cash paid ($146 million), down from $2,985 million; the equity statement shows $123 million of Class B shares repurchased, which is not used. GEOGRAPHY: rows copied from the segment note. The 'Corporate' column (revenues of $2 million, mainly foreign-currency hedge results) is omitted, so the segments sum to $46.39 billion against the reported total of $46.40 billion. Global Brand Divisions (licensing) and Converse are not geographic.
